documented_architecture.source_type: 1983 National Register nomination, section 7 description and section 8 significance
facts: Original 1899 Alfalfa Saloon used the southwest corner entrance with both floors truncated at the corner.
Circa 1910 retail conversion introduced plate-glass storefronts; upper story retained truncated corner.
Second-floor windows described as segmentally arched.
First-floor ceiling described as fourteen feet high.
Metal marquee added to Yakima Avenue elevation in the 1920s.
1983 nomination states building interior connected to two adjacent buildings by doorways.
inference_limits: 1983 doorway connections were not identified as below ground.
The document does not establish which adjacent buildings, or date/location of these connections.
No surveyed historical elevation, footprint or underground tunnel alignment is supplied.
